A.title: Aim help at those who can't pay; fix the cap's debt rules
A.answer: No cheque for every household. In 2022 that cost £36 billion (s4). Keep Ofgem and the suppliers, but change the rules. The Government pays an automatic winter credit only to households on means-tested benefits, matched from tax and benefit records, with the council covering the old and sick who miss out. Ofgem bans debt chasing and forced prepayment meters for them until spring. Fund it by taking the old policy costs off electricity bills, worth about £60 a year (s3), and by not cutting NHS, schools or councils. It worked if household energy debt stops climbing towards £7 billion (s4) and few eligible homes are missed.

B.title: Set up a public energy arm to insulate homes and carry bills
B.answer: Make a publicly owned energy body, run by a board that includes bill-payers chosen by lot. Its first job is a fast, free insulation drive. It starts with the homes of people who can't pay, and it works through councils. It also takes over help for people in arrears, so help is aimed at need, not paid to everyone. In 2022/23 universal support cost £36 billion (s4). Household energy debt may reach £7 billion by the end of 2026 (s4). We'd know it worked if debt stops growing, cap rises hurt poorer homes less, and the board publishes homes finished and money saved each quarter.
